questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Bologna because it seemed to be a great city for students - the oldest uni in the west.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty okay

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: No assistance i think.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Find facebook groups and be prepared to write in Italian, it will give you better chances.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive. There is a housing crisis in Bologna.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived inside the walls, but it is super okay to live outside them too. And bikes are cheap!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was just an online call, very quickly done.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don't know, did not use it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very, i got the ones i wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just do it

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Courses are great, teachers are good. But be prepared for a passive learning culture. Italians are not super used to class discussion and student participation - but it is often seen as a good quality still!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: If you are BA just take the MA courses also, there are so many to choose between and it is not too difficult i promise.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More traditional. Less independent. But reading is completely up to you. A lot of courses work in a way where you don't read specific articles to prepare for a class. You just show up and teacher speaks in a certain direction (hope it makes sense!)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Gender Studies
Gender and Cultures
Introduction to Italian Culture
Italian Contemporary Performance Scene
Semiotics of Conflicts

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Alle undtages introduction to italian culture. Det kursus er så demotiverende: +100 udvekslingsstuderende der snakker sig gennem 2 timers foredrag med en (stakkels) lærer der forsøger at begå sig på engelsk. Og man kommer ikke i dybden med noget, opnår kun meget overfladisk viden på en række emner.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Hmmm ikke rigtig nogen? var forberedt på dem der kom.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grøntsager + frugt er DYRT i supermarkedet. Køb i små grønthandlere i stedet. Og apoteker er dyre (fx smertestillende).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Benyttede ikke

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Alle mulige slags, som sagt brugte jeg ikke.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Vandreture ud i bakkerne<3 Togture til små nærliggende byer. Stor udendørs bio på Piazza Maggiore om sommeren!! Mange gode koncerter på Locomotiv. Der er også mange demonstrationer at tage til! Vigtigt!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Dolomitterne, Verona, Ravenna (se mosaikkerne). Du behøver ikke tage til Milano (medmindre du er en shoppetype) og du behøver ikke tage til Rom (bare min mening).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: EASY, folk er så åbne!!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Giv dem en cigaret

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Dem jeg boede med ville ikke dele krydderier eller olie. Fik dem overtalt til toiletpapir.... Men altså dansk kollektivskultur er noget vi skal være glade for. (Og jeg har selvfølgelig venner der oplevede det stikmodsatte og havde vildt gavmilde bofæller).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
De er så afslappede, ingen er stressede, alle kommer dryssende når det passer dem (ikke til tiden) og alle falder i snak med hinanden ude i hverdagslivet - caféen, parken, supermarkedet etc. 
Vildt inspirerende!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Glæd dig! 
Du kan ikke nå det hele! 
Biografbilletter er billige!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nej, jeg tror man skal lære det hen ad vejen.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Undervisning (så politisk og reel, undervisere behandlede ikke Palæstina som et tabuemne (modsat mange på KU)). Og den her antistressede kultur, hvor det føles som om der er uendeligt mange timer på en dag.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Varmen i juni og juli. 35-39 grader er ikke for sjov.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
